entities.name: Artificial Intelligence (AI)
entities.description: Technology used to assist human employees by handling initial, repetitive, and well-codified tasks.

entities.name: Human Employees (Agents)
entities.description: Workers who perform higher-level problem-solving and unscripted tasks following AI's initial work.

concepts.name: AI-Augmented Employee Creativity
concepts.description: The phenomenon where AI assistance increases the creativity of human employees by freeing them from mundane tasks.

concepts.name: Skill-Biased AI Augmentation
concepts.description: The finding that the positive impacts of AI on creativity and performance are significantly greater for employees with higher domain expertise or job skills.

concepts.name: Sequential Division of Labor
concepts.description: A workflow design where AI handles the initial, repetitive portion of a task, and human employees handle the subsequent, unstructured portion.

claims: AI assistance in handling repetitive tasks increases employees' creativity in solving subsequent higher-level problems.
Enhanced creativity due to AI assistance leads to increased overall job performance and sales.
The positive effect of AI on employee creativity is skill-biased, meaning it is much more pronounced for higher-skilled employees.
AI assistance alters job design, leading to positive emotions and innovation for highly skilled workers, but increased stress and negative emotions for lower-skilled workers.
summary: This article investigates how artificial intelligence (AI) affects employee creativity through a sequential division of labor. Through a field experiment at a telemarketing firm, the authors demonstrate that assigning repetitive lead-generation tasks to AI increases human employees' creativity during subsequent sales persuasion, thereby boosting sales. Crucially, this AI-augmented creativity is skill-biased, primarily benefiting higher-skilled employees. Qualitative interviews further reveal that this job design change fosters positive emotions and innovative problem-solving in experts, while often causing stress and demoralization among lower-skilled workers.
